newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Kucan urges Slovenia to resolve pressing problems.
newsitem.headline: Kucan urges Slovenia to resolve pressing problems.

text.p: Slovenian President Milan Kucan, looking back on six years of independence in the former Yugoslav republic, said on Monday the country had made much progress but crucial questions remained unsolved.

"Slovenia's decison for independence has paid off, not because Slovenia had no other alternative but because this alternative proved to be the good one," Kucan, told a news conference marking the anniversary of Slovenian independence.
But he warned that rising unemployment and the failure of the government and employers to reach an agreement on workers' social benefits were affecting public self confidence.
Unemployment in the tiny Alpine republic rose to 14.3 percent in April from 13.8 percent in April last year.
Kucan also urged political parties to change the constitution in line with EU standards as soon as possible so the country can ratify the EU association agreement, signed a year ago.
The constitutional court has ordered parliament to change the constitution to allow foreigners to own real estate in Slovenia before it ratifies the association accord.
Kucan said the outcome of Slovenia's bid for membership of the EU and NATO lay in the hands of the country's politicians and if it failed they would be to blame.
